attempted_method_description: treatment_class dynamic_location_price does not permit spatial_derivation (data/policy/local-54-indicator-contract.json). The only route to a constituency value would be a genuine EPRA publication at constituency/station granularity, so this review re-verifies EPRA's current pricing-town regulatory structure (rather than assuming the existing county-level Sprint 1 methodology still holds) using the live pricing cycle current at the time of review.

decisions.period_label: 15 September 2026 - 14 October 2026 EPRA pricing cycle · P31 constituency review
decisions.source: Energy & Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) — maximum retail petroleum prices notice
decisions.reason: EPRA sets maximum retail Super Petrol prices under Section 101(y) of the Petroleum Act 2019 and Legal Notice No. 192 of 2022 for a small, named set of designated pricing towns, not per petrol station, ward or constituency. This is the same structure this project already documented and validated at county level (data/sprint1/README.md, data/sprint1/VALIDATION.md, scripts/p28/validate-epra-fuel-provenance.mjs), where 45 of 47 county display slots carry an explicitly labelled Badge C 'representative pricing town, not a county average' proxy and none is presented as a direct county or sub-county value. This P31 review re-verified the structure against the live 15 September-14 October 2026 EPRA circular (independently corroborated by The Star, Pulse Kenya and K24 Digital) rather than assuming the prior cycle still applied: the same town-named schedule continues (e.g. Nairobi, Mombasa, Nakuru, Eldoret, Kisumu, Meru, Kitale, Kisii), with no reference anywhere in the notice to constituency, sub-county or ward geography, and no per-station pricing. Kenya's 290 constituencies do not correspond to EPRA's pricing-town geography: pricing towns are not aligned to, or evenly distributed across, constituency boundaries, and a single town's schedule typically covers an entire county. Under the dynamic_location_price treatment class (data/policy/local-54-indicator-contract.json), spatial_derivation is not an allowed method for this indicator in the first place, so there is no permitted construction path from the county-level pricing-town data down to constituency; only a genuine EPRA publication at that granularity could resolve this, and no prior or current EPRA cycle publishes one. No county pricing-town value is inherited, averaged or interpolated down to any constituency.
decisions.refresh_trigger: EPRA publishes maximum retail prices at constituency level, ward level or per individual petrol station under a new regulatory instrument superseding Legal Notice No. 192 of 2022 / Section 101(y) of the Petroleum Act 2019.

rules: Do not inherit, average or interpolate any county pricing-town value down to any constituency.
Do not silently describe a pricing-town value as a constituency value or constituency average.
Every closure must preserve a primary official source, reason and refresh trigger.

This closure records a genuine, diligence-backed re-verification against the current pricing cycle (not a stale assumption carried over from Sprint 1), consistent with the local-54 source-governance contract's requirement to re-check reachability/structure before reaffirming an unavailable state.
